newsitem.title: USA: U.S. concerned by action against China dissidents.
newsitem.headline: U.S. concerned by action against China dissidents.

text.p: The United States expressed deep concern on Thursday over the sentencing of a prominent Chinese dissident and apparent plans to put another on trial.

Liu Xiaobo was ordered on Wednesday to serve three years in a labor camp after he and veteran democracy activist Wang Xizhe issued a joint statement calling for the impeachment and dismissal of Communist Party chief Jiang Zemin.

On Thursday, Chinese court officials told the family of detained dissident and leader of 1989 student demonstrations Wang Dan to hire a lawyer on his behalf and gave them a day in which to do so, his mother said.
State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said the decision to arrest and sentence Liu "highlights the due process abuses in China's re-education-through-labor system."
"The United States is very concerned about this reported detention of a respected individual," Burns told a news briefing.
"It underscores the gross intolerance in China for the airing of divergent political views, no matter how peacefully these views are expressed -- in this case, very peacefully."
Burns said Washington was also "deeply concerned" about the reported decision to charge Wang in a case which he said had been raised by the top U.S. officials with senior Chinese leaders.
"We're very concerned about the conditions under which he is being held. And we will continue to follow this case as well as Mr. Liu's case, and others," Burns said.
He urged the Chinese government to release without delay all dissidents who were being held in Chinese jails solely because of their peacefully expressed political views.
Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang, commenting earlier in Beijing on reports of U.S. concern over Wang Dan's plight, told the United States not to interfere in China's internal affairs.
U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher will visit China on Nov. 21-22 and Burns said he would raise human rights issues, as he has in previous meetings with Chinese leaders.
